readerAnswers.event: A September 4 paper in Nature Communications reports an AI system that predicts later liver spread after stomach-cancer surgery. It studied 1,878 people with cancer that had spread into nearby tissue or lymph nodes, called locally advanced cancer. In these records, combining image patterns and clinical information outperformed clinical information alone at distinguishing those who later had liver spread from those who did not.
readerAnswers.mechanism: A model is a learned system that turns information into a prediction. This one combines pre-surgery CT scans—detailed internal images—with microscope images of tissue removed during surgery and clinical details. The team used some patients’ records and known later outcomes to learn which combinations went with later liver spread, then checked the prediction on separate patient groups.
readerAnswers.limit: The study did not test whether using its score to guide care improved patient outcomes. We have not verified a patient-ready service. It is research to understand, not a reason to change treatment.
readerAnswers.context: Most records came from Chinese hospitals, and performance varied by treatment group. The authors call for wider international testing and report practical implementation challenges. Funding includes public programmes and a Hengrui pharmaceutical research partnership; the authors declare no competing interests. We have not verified an independent replication.
readerAnswers.action: When a health headline says AI “helps”, try asking: Did it predict more accurately, or did using it improve what happened to patients? If a tool is being considered for your care, another useful question is how well it was tested with women and people in your situation. Those questions help you join the conversation with your care team.

terms.risk: For a patient, a false alarm could lead to unnecessary intervention; a missed warning could give false reassurance. A useful evaluation therefore asks what decisions people make with a prediction and what those decisions do. Risk means a chance, not a certainty. A higher score should not be read as a personal verdict.

terms.supervised learning: Learning from examples paired with known answers is called supervised learning. Explore that idea in the opening of AI Fundamentals 101, section 3.4. It explains why knowing what happened in past examples can help train a prediction; medical usefulness still needs its own evidence.

explainBack: The team learned from existing patient information paired with what later happened and tested the prediction on other groups. Better prediction does not show that using its score to choose care helps patients; the source trial was about chemotherapy, not AI-guided decisions.
unseenTransfer: A company predicts which staff are likely to leave. Even if its prediction is accurate, that does not demonstrate that the retention programme it recommends reduces departures; that intervention needs a separate evaluation of actual results and possible harms.
